name: Fiji
prevalence_note: The Reserve Bank of Fiji has twice warned, in 2024 and 2025, against social-media investment pitches, including an unapproved Facebook scheme named Elite Society and a later AI-generated video that falsely presents the Governor as backing an automatic trading platform run by the Bank. The Consumer Council of Fiji has separately described callers who pose as the Police Cybercrime Unit, send a link, then claim a bank account is blocked in order to steal login details.
cross_border_note: Fiji uses +679. The 2025 Reserve Bank notice says the false Governor video has circulated on digital platforms in Fiji and abroad, so a clip that appears to come from the central bank, or digits that merely resemble a Suva line, still do not show that the Bank or the Police made the approach.

scams.name: AI video falsely showing the Reserve Bank Governor promoting an automatic trading scheme
scams.name_en: Reserve Bank of Fiji 2025 warning: an AI-generated video fabricates the Governor's endorsement of an automatic-trading platform, then agents seek personal data through a link or a telephone pitch
context_keywords: agent asking for a registration link

red_flag_keywords.text: the Governor is promoting this platform
click the link to open an RBF trading account
automatic trades administered by the Bank
telephone agent of the investment platform

scams.signals_en: A video circulating on social and other digital channels appears to show the Reserve Bank Governor recommending an automatic trading product said to be run by the Bank. The Bank says the remarks were generated by AI, that it does not run or endorse such a platform, and that people fronting as agents may ask the viewer to open a link and hand over personal information, or may follow up by telephone.
scams.legit_en: The Reserve Bank of Fiji does not operate or endorse an automatic-trading product for the public, and it does not recruit investors through social-media videos or cold calls. A genuine enquiry about whether a scheme is approved goes to the Bank through the contact path published on rbf.gov.fj, not through a link or number attached to the clip.
bait_tactics: Say any investment will be confirmed with the Reserve Bank using the contact details on its own website, not a link under the video.
Ask the caller to name the licence or Companies Act approval the platform claims to hold, and decline to give personal details on the same call.
Refuse to treat a social-media clip as an official Reserve Bank statement, even when the voice or face resembles the Governor.

scams.name: Unapproved Elite Society Facebook investment recruitment
scams.name_en: Reserve Bank of Fiji and FCCC 2024 warning: Elite Society and similar social-media schemes recruit members on Facebook without Reserve Bank approval under the Companies Act
context_keywords: Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission alert

red_flag_keywords.text: join Elite Society to earn returns
pay a membership contribution on Facebook
scheme not approved by the Reserve Bank
recruit friends into the investment group

scams.signals_en: After an FCCC media release, the Reserve Bank warned that a Facebook operation called Elite Society, like other social-media investment invitations, is not approved by the Bank. Schemes that pool members' money for a promised benefit, without day-to-day control by those members, are managed investment schemes that must be approved under the Companies Act 2015.
scams.legit_en: A lawful managed investment scheme in Fiji is one the Reserve Bank has approved. The Bank invites the public to ask it whether a social-media offer is legitimate before any money is paid into a Facebook group or to an unapproved promoter.
bait_tactics: Say the Facebook offer will be referred to the Reserve Bank for a check on approval before any contribution is paid.
Ask who holds day-to-day control of the pooled money, and why the scheme does not appear on an official approval list.
Decline to recruit relatives into the group until the Bank has confirmed that it is a licensed scheme.

scams.name: Caller posing as the Fiji Police Cybercrime Unit to steal banking logins
scams.name_en: Consumer Council of Fiji warning: a caller claims to be from the Police Cybercrime Unit, sends a link, then says a bank account is blocked and harvests login details
context_keywords: number placed on a list by mistake
link sent to unblock the account

red_flag_keywords.text: give your banking login to unblock the account
click this Police link to leave the list
Cybercrime Unit needs your password now
your mobile was listed by mistake

scams.signals_en: The Consumer Council describes a call in which someone pretends to be from the Police Cybercrime Unit, says a mobile number was put on a list in error, and sends a link. A later call claims the person's bank account has been blocked and must be unblocked by handing over login credentials; the stolen access is then used to empty the account, and in the reported case the person's Facebook account was also taken over to ask friends for a mobile-wallet transfer.
scams.legit_en: The Consumer Council states that the Fiji Police Force and the Cybercrime Unit do not ask for login credentials, banking details or other personal information over the telephone, and do not tell people to follow a link. A real police matter is handled through official Police channels or, if needed, in person.
bait_tactics: End the unexpected call and say a Police matter will be taken up only at a published Fiji Police channel, never via a number or link supplied by the caller.
Refuse to type a banking password or one-time code into a page that arrived during the call.
Tell friends, if a sudden mobile-wallet request appears from a hijacked social account, to confirm the emergency in person or on a familiar number before sending money.
